w: Home to the Black Madonna of Czestochowa, an icon credited with miraculous powers, this fortified monastery has drawn Polish pilgrims for centuries as the country's foremost shrine to the Virgin Mary. It holds official status as one of Poland's national Historic Monuments, tracked by the National Heritage Board.
s: Shrine of the Black Madonna, Poland's top pilgrimage site
_facts: Shrine to the Virgin Mary, Poland's leading pilgrimage site
Houses the Black Madonna of Czestochowa icon
Designated a Polish national Historic Monument

n: Cathedral Basilica of the Holy Family, Częstochowa
w: Designed by Konstanty Wojciechowski and built 1901-1927 on the site of a cemetery used from 1825 to 1898, this neo-Gothic three-nave basilica became the cathedral of the Czestochowa diocese in 1925 and the metropolitan church of its province in 1992. Its Chapel of Our Lady of Czestochowa holds a bishops' crypt.
s: A neo-Gothic cathedral built over a former cemetery
_facts: Metropolitan church of the province since 1992
Chapel of Our Lady of Czestochowa holds a bishops' crypt

n: Orthodox Church of the Icon of Our Lady of Częstochowa
w: Ground broke in 1994 on a design by Bialystok architect Michal Balasz, and the cornerstone was blessed by Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew I himself. By 2009 the bells, windows and facade were finished, though the interior decoration remained incomplete.
s: An Orthodox church blessed by the Ecumenical Patriarch
_facts: Construction began 1994, designed by Michal Balasz
Cornerstone blessed by Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew I
Facade complete by 2009, interior still unfinished

w: Once called Stara Gora, this 295-meter rise in the Upper Warta Depression carries the Jasna Gora Monastery on its northeastern summit. Administratively it straddles two districts, Podjasnogorska and Czestochowka-Parkitka - a single hill split by a line on the map, with a national shrine sitting on top of it.
s: The 295m hill the Jasna Gora shrine sits on
_facts: Formerly known as Stara Gora Hill
Split between Podjasnogorska and Czestochowka-Parkitka districts

w: Tucked onto the first floor of Czestochowa Stradom railway station, this museum has told the story of Polish rail since its ceremonial opening on 23 March 2001 - a working station doubling as an archive of the trains that built it.
s: A rail museum inside a working station building

w: Staszic Park and 3 May Park wrap the eastern flank of the Jasna Gora Monastery, their boundaries laid out between 1819 and 1826 and developed from 1843. Together with Sienkiewicz Avenue they cover 11.8 hectares, hold exhibition pavilions run by the Czestochowa Museum, and carry historic-monument status.
s: Two historic parks flanking the Jasna Gora shrine
_facts: Exhibition pavilions run by the Czestochowa Museum
